title: The Offshore Tax Grab

The Offshore Tax Grab

Xiaoxi Zhang, Christopher Beddor

Gavekal Dragonomics | 10 Aug 2026

In recent months, many people across China have received a text message with a “friendly reminder” from their local tax bureau: that they must declare and pay taxes on all income from offshore assets. Their reactions, documented in numerous social-media posts, have ranged from surprise to shock and panic: many taxpayers have never reported offshore investment income, relying on a long history of lax enforcement. Now, it’s clear that enforcement is tightening up as the tax authorities work to boost revenue and squeeze the common tax dodges used by high-income households. While the government has been building the infrastructure for better enforcement for years, its latest actions go beyond enforcing existing rules to change some long-accepted tax practices.China’s income-tax law has for decades required residents to pay a 20% tax on interest, dividends and gains from asset sales, regardless of whether the income is inside China or abroad. In practice, that tax has rarely been enforced on offshore investment income, and several exemptions mean that individuals pay little tax on domestic investment income as well. But this dynamic started to change in 2024, when tax authorities reportedly demanded that some individuals with especially large foreign-asset holdings pay the levy, including for some earlier years.
